summary: Unauthorized service-account API keys created after third-party CI OAuth grant via Slack link
description:
Issue summary: Multiple ephemeral API keys were observed being issued for a Redwood service account (sa-ingest-01) in a short time window. Initial alert triggered by anomalous token creation rate from CI-related IP ranges and a spike in privileged ingest.put() calls. Investigation showed a recent OAuth grant to a third-party CI integration (BuildPulse) initiated from a Slack message link.

Impact: Potential unauthorized access to internal ingest pipelines and telemetry. No confirmed exfiltration of PII; elevated write activity to event_ingest.topic detected. Affecting one service account: sa-ingest-01. Scope currently limited to prod us-east cluster.

Timeline: 2026-03-12 09:03 UTC - SRE alert for unusual token issuance rate for sa-ingest-01. 2026-03-12 09:08 UTC - Support ticket created by oncall after Slack reports of strange message from #dev-integrations. 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - OAuth grant recorded: external app BuildPulse (app_id: bp-73a2) was authorized by user e.id=shawn.kim@redwood.com via slack-clicked link. 2026-03-12 09:25-09:40 UTC - Automated CI runner IPs issued three api-keys for sa-ingest-01 and performed high-volume ingest.put() calls.

Environment: prod-us-east, service: ingest, service-account: sa-ingest-01, integration: BuildPulse (third-party CI), communication vector: Slack message with link.

Detection: Alert rule "token-issuance-rate" fired (threshold 5 tokens/min) in Alerting -> Security. SRE observed tokens created by our token-service with user_agent header matching BuildPulse and originating from ci-runner-ops static IPs. Audit logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q=token-service%20sa-ingest-01%20%22bp-73a2%22 (internal link).

Steps to reproduce (observed): 1) A user clicked a Slack message link in #dev-integrations that redirected to BuildPulse OAuth consent. 2) OAuth granted BuildPulse limited scopes including token:create for service accounts via a delegated CI flow. 3) BuildPulse used CI runners to call our token-service and created short-lived API keys bound to sa-ingest-01. 4) CI job triggered high-volume ingest calls.

Evidence collected: - Token-service issuance logs (timestamps and request ids) - CI runner IP connection logs - Slack message permalink: https://slack.redwood.internal/archives/C013XXXX/p1678698623000200 - BuildPulse OAuth audit entry in admin-portal (bp-73a2) - stacktrace of ingest.put() call anomalies - Screen capture of OAuth consent prompt cached in SSO audit.

Initial containment actions taken: - Disabled BuildPulse app oauth client in internal oauth admin at 09:32 UTC. - Rotated the tokens for sa-ingest-01 and revoked all active API keys at 09:40 UTC. - Temporarily blocked CI runner IPs in firewall allowlist while we validate runner images. - Issued org-wide Slack advisory to not click unfamiliar build/ci links and to report messages to #security.

Open questions: - Which user account authorized BuildPulse and did they have permission to grant service-account scopes? (initially appears to be shawn.kim@redwood.com) - Were any persisted credentials or configuration files in CI systems leaked to BuildPulse? - Did the BuildPulse app escalate beyond intended scopes?

Required next steps: 1) SRE to audit all token issuances for the last 48 hours across service accounts. 2) Identity team to review OAuth consent policy and restrict service-account scope grants to a allowlist of apps. 3) SecOps to run a forensic snapshot of affected CI runner instances. 4) Postmortem and communication template for leadership and legal.

2026-03-12 09:30 Alexei Petrov (SRE): Confirmed token issuance spike. Found OAuth client id bp-73a2 in token request user_agent. Blocking app client as precaution.
2026-03-12 09:36 Dani Lopez (IAM): Revoked existing API keys for sa-ingest-01 and rotated service account creds. Added immediate firewall rule to block CI runner subnet.
2026-03-12 10:05 Maria Chen (SecOps): Starting forensic snapshot of ci-runner-ops-1 and requested snapshots from cloud provider. Gathering container images and job manifests.

2026-03-12 11:00 Shawn Kim (Developer): I clicked a Slack link from #dev-integrations to accept a BuildPulse integration. I thought this was a team-initiated integration. I'm available to help provide timestamps and my browser history.
2026-03-12 12:15 Ravi Patel (Identity): We're drafting a temporary policy: disallow oauth for service-account scopes unless app is in allowlist. Will PR changes to oauth admin next.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: A malicious or misconfigured BuildPulse connector requested and obtained excessive delegated scopes due to overly broad consent screen, enabling token: create for service accounts.
Logs show three api keys created at 09:25, 09:31, 09:39 UTC. Each key had a 10m TTL and was used for 2-10k ingest.put() calls before revocation.
No downstream data export detected in outbound egress logs; however high-volume writes could have masked other activity. Need to preserve logs for longer retention window.
User shawn.kim had team_admin role which allowed him to approve third-party integrations in the past; identity policy gap identified.
CI runner images currently under analysis for potential compromised tokens or leaked config; preliminary volume indicates automated job triggered by BuildPulse webhook.
Correlating Slack permalink timestamps with oauth grant shows click at 09:19:47 UTC; oauth token exchange at 09:19:58 UTC.
Recommend immediate hardening: require MFA for consent to any app requesting service-account scopes; add admin approval flow for service-account oauth grants.
resolution: Containment completed: BuildPulse oauth client disabled, all active API keys for sa-ingest-01 revoked, CI runner IPs blocked. Ongoing forensic analysis of CI runners and token-service audit. Identity team implementing temporary allowlist and admin-approval flow for service-account OAuth grants. Final postmortem to be produced after full investigation.
